newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa rand/bonds closing report.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa rand/bonds closing report.

text.p: A late round of offshore dollar selling provided the only highlight to what was generally a dismal day on the rand market on Monday, helping it firm just under one cent against the dollar.

Shortly after 1400 GMT, the rand was at 4.4240/4270 against the dollar from 4.4335/4365 at 1400 GMT on Thursday. It had traded in a 4.4270 to 4.4380 range for most of the day, before strengthening about 10 minutes before the local close.
In after-hours trade, it touched a day's strongest level of 4.4220 bid.
On the whole, though, dealers described the day's activity as quiet, lethargic and directionless.

The lethargy was pinned on two factors, one being that local markets will be closed on Friday for the Easter break and the other being that players had devoted most of their attention to the last day of the third and final cricket test match being played between South Africa and Australia.
What interest there was on the day was pinned to local bank two-way trading and importer dollar demand.
The month-end dollar demand helped one-year forward rates to their lowest levels since September 24 1996. They were last quoted at 41.50 points from 42.25 points on Thursday.
Dealers said that despite the spot rand's late-found strength on the day, more importer demand was expected to surface as the week as they sought to cover their month-end commitments.
However, dealers said the Reserve Bank's apparent desire to halt any advance above the 4.44 level was likely to keep the rand in a 4.4250 to 4.44 range for the rest of the week.
Against sterling, cable's advance to close to the 1.61 level pushed the rand about five cents weaker to leave it at 7.1206/1299 from 7.0760/0862 previously.
The local unit was also quoted at 0.3811/3815 marks from 0.3782/3786 as the dollar recovered some of its recent losses against the German currency.

On the bond market, yields were constrained to a five point range as players held to the sidelines ahead of a key U.S. Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) meeting on Tuesday as well as the release of local economic indicators later in the week.
Dealers said anticipation of a Fed tightening on Tuesday had kept speculators at bay, although the move had mostly been discounted by the market.
"There is an 80 percent probability of a 25-point hike," a trader said.
Dealers said the market would also look to glean direction from February trade and consumer inflation data, as well as latest exchequer data scheduled for release on Tuesday.

A Reuters consensus poll of economists forecast said the trade balance, which is due sometime this week, is expected to show a 1.04 billion rand surplus compared with a 0.5 billion rand surplus in January.
Consumer inflation, due out at 0900 GMT on Thursday, is expected to show a 0.45 percent month-on-month increase compared with 1.3 percent previously.
On the money market, three-month deposit rates held steady at 16.50 to 16.55 percent offered, while the 90-day BA rate maintained its recent 15.90 to 16.10 percent range.
The Reserve Bank said the money market shortage stood at 10.078 billion rand on Saturday from 10.334 billion rand on Thursday.
The Bond Exchange said that foreigners sold a net 100.91 million rand's worth of South African bonds on Thursday after selling 317.59 million rand's worth on Wednesday.
Nominal cumulative volumes on Thursday, settlement day, amounted to 42.51 billion rand from 7.59 billion rand on Wednesday.
-- Paul Richardson, Johannesburg newsroom 27 11 482 1003
